audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Sett/Sett/Sett/Skill/Sett/Skill/Skill. The already-audited mirror (zac__sett) settled this chart as Sett, Skill, Sett, Zac, Sett, Zac, Zac.
audit.why: Restating the mirror's finding from Sett's side rather than re-deriving it: level 2 is even because Unstable Matter is a flat 5s percent-max-health hit, and from levels 4-5 onward Cell Division refunds the trades Sett wins.
audit.corrected: Sett / Skill / Sett / Zac / Sett / Zac / Zac — identical to the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why and phases[6].why credited Stridebreaker and Sterak's as Sett-favoured spikes in rows that belong to Zac.
audit.why: Unstable Matter deals a percentage of the TARGET's maximum health, so Sterak's Gage and Heartsteel actively feed Zac's damage. And Cell Division revives him from four bloblets, so a clean burst kill is not a kill.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten — max-health items called out as feeding his W, and the revive stated at 2+ items.

audit.whatIsWrong: The ultimate was written 'Let's Bounce' (packet flagged it), no cooldown appeared anywhere in the matchup, and the Facebreaker stun condition was never stated.
audit.why: The ability is Let's Bounce! (120/105/90s, four bounces). Elastic Slingshot is 21s at rank 1 falling to 9s — that gap is the whole engage window. And Facebreaker only stuns when it grabs enemies on opposite sides of Sett, exactly as the mirror recorded; caught alone, Zac is only slowed.
audit.corrected: Name fixed, E and W cooldowns added, and the stun condition restated from the mirror.

edits.before: Q gives move speed toward Zac and two empowered punches. Take short Q trades and back off before he can answer with Elastic Slingshot.
edits.after: Unstable Matter (W) is a flat 5s and burns a percentage of your max health, so level 2 is even. Trade in the gap right after it fires.

edits.before: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier, but Zac has his core tools too. Keep the grit bar honest: trade in, W-shield his return damage, out.
edits.after: Cell Division sheds a blob every time an ability hits you, and he eats them back. Stand on every blob or the trade you won gets refunded.

edits.before: Stridebreaker fixes your only weakness — sticking to Zac. Shove, recall on the spike, and force the next trade before he matches your item.
edits.after: His first health item is the turn — Unstable Matter scales off your max health, so Sterak's and Heartsteel feed it. Buy armour and anti-heal.

edits.before: Sterak's makes your all-in nearly unburstable. Fights are decided by whether you cash a max-grit W — track Elastic Slingshot and commit on the gap.
edits.after: Two items in Zac is a teamfight engage you cannot burst: Cell Division revives him off four bloblets. Kill the blobs, not just the body.

edits.before: - Zac Elastic Slingshot: matchup-defining — His engage. Punish the cooldown. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Zac Elastic Slingshot (E): 21s at rank 1, 9s at rank 5 — his only engage. - Unstable Matter (W): flat 5s.

edits.before: Level 2 Sett keeps the lead with stronger base damage before Zac's sustain matters.
edits.after: Level 2 is even: Unstable Matter (W) is a 5s percent-health hit that ignores your armour.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 Sett out-trades while denying blobs so Zac can't heal the damage back.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 Zac's blobs heal back everything you land unless you stand on every one.

edits.before: First item Sett's bruiser brawl beats Zac's early tank frame in a duel.
edits.after: First item Zac's health stack turns Unstable Matter into real percent damage.

edits.before: R The Show Stopper answers Zac's R Let's Bounce — if he ults to knock you up, your Grit shield eats it and you E-pull plus ult him back. Kill him before he can retreat to pick up his four blobs and revive via passive.
edits.after: Let's Bounce! (R) is 120s at rank 1 and knocks up on four bounces — your Grit shield eats the first one. Facebreaker only stuns when it grabs enemies on both sides of you, so pull him across your minions.

notes: The mirror (zac__sett) was already audited, so its chart was adopted verbatim rather than the packet levelChart, which still reads Sett through Level 6 — the two disagree at rows 1, 3 and 5 and the mirror wins. Sett's Haymaker is true damage only in the CENTRE (physical on the sides), per the mirror's second finding; no field in this matchup claimed otherwise, so nothing needed changing for it.
